verdictStatement: Every finding from both v7 reviewers is repaired, and three of the seven match their repair texts clause for clause rather than in spirit. My blocker is gone at its root: terminal is now a property of the carrier rather than of an event, the FIRST of the two terminalizing events emits the single marker and later events are explicit no-ops, and the three marker-less states are gathered into a named failClosedNoAppend branch that appends nothing. The live-pointer defect I have raised three times is fixed structurally rather than re-pointed — both fields now name 'the remeasurement block whose standing is LIVE', which cannot go stale when v9 adds another block, and I verified exactly one block carries that standing. The succession discipline holds for the fourth generation: 46 changed paths, zero off-roster, 160 of 160 non-roster paths byte-identical. What remains is confined to the fail-closed branch that v8 introduced. Of its three member states, two say plainly that they are permanent and one does not, and the durable fact that the branch says keeps a carrier fail-closed is never placed for the witnessless-restore case — in an artifact whose stated purpose is to assign or expressly reserve every named durable byte. Neither defect is a contradiction and neither touches the supersession, the placement, or the owner gate. Both are one-clause edits.

shouldFix.title: Two of the three failClosedNoAppend states declare themselves permanent and lossOrCapacity does not, leaving it unclear whether a capacity boundary ends the generation or merely pauses it
shouldFix.subjectQuote: lossOrCapacity: 'At any storage-loss or capacity boundary the writer fail-closes and refuses new appends. It MUST NOT drop or compact away order to make room.'

measurement.theAsymmetry: failClosedNoAppend classes three states as 'already non-appending terminal-equivalent states': lossOrCapacity, witnessless-restore revocation, and FROZEN-UNDER-OVERTURN. Two of the three say permanence in their own clause — backupRestore: 'that grant generation is permanently revoked (failClosedNoAppend)'; reversibility: 'no new appends' with the only exit gated behind a separately authorized owner-concurred migration and a user-express D-096 (A) grant. lossOrCapacity says neither 'permanent' nor anything about recovery.
measurement.whyTheReadingMatters: A capacity boundary is prototypically transient — space is freed and the writer can append again. If lossOrCapacity is transient, then it is not terminal-equivalent, and the failClosedNoAppend branch applies to it wrongly: a projectPurge or grantGenerationClosure arriving during the fail-closed window is a no-op that appends no marker and sets no TERMINAL state, so once capacity recovers the carrier is open and appendable although the project has been purged or the generation closed. If instead lossOrCapacity is permanent, then a transient disk-full condition permanently kills the grant generation — a severe consequence stated nowhere in the branch that produces it.
measurement.whatTheArtifactAsserts: By classing it terminal-equivalent, failClosedNoAppend implies the second reading. lossOrCapacity's own text supports the first. The artifact never resolves which.

shouldFix.whatIsNotWrong: The conservative posture is right and I am not asking for it to be softened: 'MUST NOT drop or compact away order to make room' is the correct answer at a capacity boundary and was already the strongest clause in v6's block. The state machine that failClosedNoAppend introduces is a genuine repair of my v7 blocker. This is about one branch's permanence, not the branch's existence.
shouldFix.whyItStillMatters: terminalIs makes terminal a property of the carrier, so every state feeding that property must be determinate. Under the transient reading the artifact permits a purged carrier to reopen, which is the exact class of outcome the FIRST-wins rule was added to prevent; under the permanent reading it imposes an irreversible consequence without disclosing it. A harness author cannot pick between them from the bytes.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: State permanence in the lossOrCapacity clause the way the other two branches do. If it is permanent, say so and say that the generation continues only as a new carrier. If it is recoverable, remove it from failClosedNoAppend and state what happens to a purge or closure that arrived while the writer was fail-closed — which is the case the FIRST-wins rule currently leaves without a marker.

shouldFix.title: failClosedNoAppend asserts that a standing is the durable fact keeping a carrier fail-closed, but for the witnessless-restore case no durable byte is placed to hold it — in an artifact whose purpose is to place every named durable byte
shouldFix.subjectQuote: The durable fact that keeps them fail-closed is that standing itself; this artifact does not mint a second marker class.

measurement.theThreeStandingsAreNotAlike: FROZEN-UNDER-OVERTURN has a durable external carrier — it follows from the coordinator's overturn recording, which is a recorded act. lossOrCapacity is arguably observable from the storage condition while it lasts. Witnessless-restore revocation has neither: it is a property of an event that has already finished, and the artifact declines to mint both the witness class ('This artifact does not mint the witness class') and any marker for it ('does not mint a second marker class').
measurement.theConsequence: After a witnessless restore the generation is revoked, but nothing in the carrier records that. On the next host start the writer sees a carrier whose tail parses and whose terminal marker is absent, which is indistinguishable from a healthy open carrier — so it may resume appends on a generation the contract says is permanently revoked. That is the tail-loss hazard the revocation exists to prevent, re-entered through restart rather than through restore.
measurement.againstTheArtifactsOwnPurpose: /purpose commits this artifact to 'assigns or expressly reserves every named durable byte the preview writes or a sibling contract routes here'. The revoked standing is a durable fact the design names and relies on. It is neither assigned a class nor EXPRESSLY-RESERVED to another row, while eleven other byte-sets in bytePlacement are one or the other.

shouldFix.whatIsNotWrong: Declining to mint the witness class is a legitimate and disclosed choice — it is recorded in foldingNotes, it is the branch Codex's v6 B1 permitted, and it is why every restore revokes rather than guessing (M-19). I am not asking for the witness to be minted, and I am not attacking the revocation rule, which is correct. The gap is only that the artifact asserts durability for a standing it does not place.
shouldFix.whyItStillMatters: This is a state-class contract; placing the durable bytes a design depends on is precisely its subject, and it discharges that obligation carefully everywhere else — including by reservation where it does not want to decide. Asserting 'the durable fact … is that standing itself' without naming where the standing lives is the one place the artifact relies on a durable fact it has not placed.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Either place it — a revoked/standing record inside the existing grant-journal carrier is not a 'second marker class' if it is the same terminal marker written at revocation — or EXPRESSLY-RESERVE the revoked-standing bytes to the row that will own them (DR-105 for generation standing, or DR-107 for on-disk encoding), in the same form used for the monotonic trust store. Alternatively state that revocation's durability rides the witness class and is therefore not established until that class exists, which would be an honest disclosure rather than an assertion.

coordinatorNote: No blockers, and the two remaining items sit entirely inside the branch v8 added. That is worth saying plainly: the terminalization state machine is a real repair of a real defect, and the fact that the only findings left are about the edges of that machine rather than about the supersession, the placement, the owner set or the D-096 (A) gate is the honest measure of where this row now stands. Both items are the same shape — a state the design relies on whose properties are asserted rather than stated. S-1 is one clause saying whether a capacity fail-close is permanent; S-2 is one clause saying where a revoked generation's standing durably lives, or reserving those bytes to the row that will own them, exactly as the monotonic trust store is reserved. I would flag S-2 as the one worth a moment's thought rather than a mechanical fix: it is the only place in the artifact where a durable fact is depended upon without being placed, and placing it may be as small as noting that the existing terminal marker is written at revocation. I did not read the other current v8 reviewer, did not edit the subject or the prompt, did not edit file 08 or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, did not apply SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL, did not mint a D-096 (A) grant, did not treat SC-OPS as a grant journal outside the subject's named supersession, and did not commit.
